name: Hong Kong Open
stakes: With top contenders exiting in the semifinals, this Hong Kong Open served as a crucial test of form and a valuable gauge of India's standing against global elite ahead of upcoming major tournaments.
summary:
India's campaign at the Hong Kong Open has seen its top contenders fall in the semifinals, bringing an end to what had been a promising run for some. **Lakshya Sen**, riding a phenomenal 13-match winning streak after clinching back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and Japan Masters, ultimately found his momentum halted by Anders Antonsen in a straight-games defeat. It’s a tough exit for Sen, who had shown incredible form leading into this Super 500 event.

Similarly, India's premier men's doubles pair, **Satwik & Chirag**, also saw their journey conclude in the penultimate round. The world No. 6 duo battled hard but ultimately succumbed to Malaysia's eighth-seeded pair, Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun, in a closely contested match. While the semifinals mark the end of the road for these key Indian entries, the experience gained against top-tier opponents at a Super 500 event is invaluable. Other Indian shuttlers like PV Sindhu, HS Prannoy, Treesa & Gayatri, and Malvika Bansod were also part of the contingent, though their paths through the draw were less highlighted in the later stages of the tournament.
